title: Dynamic Legal Document Summarization at Scale
business: A legal technology firm providing automated contract review services for thousands of concurrent corporate clients.
problem: The firm faces significant bottlenecks during peak hours when thousands of legal documents are submitted simultaneously for summarization, leading to request timeouts and inefficient GPU memory utilization due to fragmented KV cache allocation.
solution: By deploying vLLM, the firm leverages PagedAttention to manage KV cache memory in non-contiguous blocks, effectively eliminating memory fragmentation. This allows the system to handle high-concurrency request streams through continuous batching, where incoming requests are dynamically grouped into the execution pipeline without waiting for previous batches to complete.
steps: Configure the vLLM OpenAI-compatible API server to host the chosen legal-domain LLM.
Enable PagedAttention settings to optimize memory allocation for long-context legal documents.
Implement continuous batching to ensure that new document summarization requests are injected into the GPU processing queue as soon as capacity becomes available.
Utilize automatic prefix caching to store common legal boilerplate structures, reducing redundant computation across similar contract types.
outcome: The system achieves a more consistent request processing flow, allowing the firm to maintain high throughput during document submission spikes without requiring additional hardware provisioning.
limitation: A primary trade-off is the increased complexity in monitoring memory pressure when using aggressive batching; if the KV cache block size is misconfigured relative to the document length, the system may experience out-of-memory errors, which can be diagnosed by monitoring the vLLM metrics for block eviction rates.

# Define parameters for summarization

# Process batch of documents
outputs = llm.generate(prompts, sampling_params)
